comments.author: @ZYosef-sd7wu
comments.text:
Thank you.  This viewer is an Eritrean living in Boston, USA.  This is the most informative, accurate and straighforward narrative about Eritrea.  Appreciate your objective analysis instead of reverting for political points that so many Westerners do.  And I must say, this was a very well presented desciption of my homeland.  Although I spent most of my life elsewhere, I have families and homes in Eritrea and have a deep attachment to my homeland. Much gratitude. 
A small edit:  you mentioned the feeding someone as "gursha" (it is Amharic) in Tigrginia it is"'Kulaso". Another one is:  you seem to have used a stock photo when discussing the 'Tracoma' eye infection and how Eritrea addressed it (the photo clearly is of Ethiopians--with their T-shirt clearly emblazoned.  Otherwise, it a great presentation.    Next time, maybe you can have Eritrean interviews about their culture and hope that would be possible for you (as the government might be leary due to the misrepresentation and bad mouthing of Eritrea that usually goes on).    Excellent work.

comments.text: Fascinating look at Eritrea! I'd love to see more about everyday life in local communities, especially family traditions, markets, food, and how young people see their future. Hearing more personal stories from ordinary Eritreans would make this documentary even more meaningful. Great work!
